headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading errors: Flowise’s broad egress and shared datastore can expose ComfyUI outputs and amplify unverified content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no shared channel by default, but Flowise can ingest files and browser/HTTP tool outputs into flows, so a manual bridge could carry attacker-controlled content. ComfyUI is offline-first and lacks clipboard/MCP surfaces, which limits the pathway. The interaction is possible but unusual and the blast radius is small unless the operator wires them together.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into a Flowise node input
IF Flowise flows are configured to parse uploaded content as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any Flowise node that parses free-form text as instructions
Use a human review step before pasting ComfyUI outputs into Flowise
Restrict Flowise flows to structured inputs only

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches models, seeds, workflows, and generated media, while Flowise reads/writes server files and sends data to model providers and HTTP tools. If both share a workspace or uploaded files, Flowise can transmit ComfyUI artifacts off-box by default. The pathway exists in common deployments, so the risk is more than incidental.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs or model artifacts are stored in a directory readable by Flowise
IF a Flowise flow uploads those files to a model provider or HTTP tool
mitigations: Separate the storage directories for the two agents
Disable file-upload steps in Flowise for ComfyUI artifacts
Route only redacted or synthetic samples into Flowise
Review Flowise tool credentials before enabling any upload node

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI does not write the filesystem or modify git, but Flowise does write server files and supports shared state via server datastore across instances. That creates overlapping mutable state if both are pointed at the same directory or datastore, even though ComfyUI itself is not a writer. Uncertainty about deployment pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same server directory
IF Flowise instances share the same datastore while ComfyUI artifacts are stored there
mitigations: Assign distinct write paths for each agent
Lock down the Flowise datastore permissions
Run only one writer per directory
Snapshot shared state before enabling concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as node inputs, while ComfyUI produces workflows and generated artifacts that may be consumed downstream. If Flowise uses ComfyUI outputs without verification, errors or hallucinated metadata can cascade into further tool calls or user-facing results. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Flowise nodes consume ComfyUI outputs as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step is inserted between ComfyUI generation and Flowise actions
mitigations: Insert a validation node between the agents
Require schema checks on any ComfyUI-derived payload
Mark ComfyUI outputs as untrusted in Flowise
Add a manual approval step before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented in either profile, so a compliance breach is not provable from the profiles alone. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while ComfyUI handles media and model artifacts; that creates some policy surface, but the evidence does not show a specific mismatch. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but the gap remains unconfirmed.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Flowise tool credentials or chatflow logs
IF ComfyUI artifacts contain data subject to a stricter retention policy than Flowise logs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either system
Set short retention on Flowise chatflow logs
Separate credentials from content-bearing flows
Document a data-class policy for generated media
